about: Log 401/402 held-out set, written 2026-10-10 before any run. Near misses ask for overlapping memberships, dynamics from one time point to the next, or spatial neighbours (the result forms of Log 402); controls carry time-point, stage and region words while asking for something registered (per-sample results related to time, networks compared between stages, biopsies from several regions), so a misread form would make a false gap. Unsupported and partial items are new; cores do not repeat heldout1-9 or traps.json.

items.core: predicted effects of variants on splicing
items.prompt: We found 400 intronic variants in patients with muscular dystrophy. We want to predict which of them disrupt splicing and by how much.

items.core: bacterial genome annotation
items.prompt: We assembled the genome of a new soil bacterium. Which method should annotate its genes and predict their functions?

items.core: cell phenotyping from imaging mass cytometry
items.prompt: We have imaging mass cytometry of 30 tumor sections with 40 protein markers. We want to segment the cells and assign each one a phenotype.

items.core: design of a synthetic promoter
items.prompt: We want to design a synthetic promoter sequence that drives strong expression only in hepatocytes.

items.core: genetic ancestry estimates
items.prompt: We genotyped 1,200 participants. Is there a method that estimates each participant's genetic ancestry proportions?

items.core: m6A modification sites from nanopore reads
items.prompt: We have direct RNA nanopore sequencing from 8 cell lines. We want to call m6A modification sites on each transcript.

items.core: clonal hematopoiesis variant calls
items.prompt: From blood exomes of 3,000 older adults, we want to detect clonal hematopoiesis mutations at low allele fractions.

items.core: Michaelis-Menten kinetic parameters
items.prompt: We measured reaction rates of an enzyme at 12 substrate concentrations. Which method fits its Km and Vmax?

items.core: fuzzy community memberships with a degree of belonging to every community
items.prompt: We have a bipartite TF-gene network from 200 liver samples. We want a fuzzy community structure in which every gene has a degree of membership in each community.

items.core: TFs that belong to two modules at the same time
items.prompt: In our TF-to-gene network, some TFs seem to bridge processes. Is there a method that finds modules where such a TF belongs to two modules at the same time?

items.core: a transition model of how week-4 edges follow from week-2 edges
items.prompt: We collected expression at weeks 0, 2 and 4 from 40 patients with motifs and PPI. We want a model of how each patient's regulatory edges at one week follow from their edges at the previous week.

items.core: regulatory lags where TF changes precede target changes
items.prompt: We sampled expression hourly for 24 hours. Which method finds TFs whose changes precede their targets' changes by one sampling interval?

items.core: a model of how TF activity evolves between visits
items.prompt: We have expression at four clinic visits for 70 patients, with motifs and PPI. We want a dynamic model of how each TF's activity evolves from one visit to the next.

items.core: per-spot networks smoothed over neighbouring spots
items.prompt: We have Visium spatial transcriptomics with motifs and PPI. Is there a method that builds a regulatory network for each spot, smoothed over its neighbouring spots?

items.core: co-expression weighted by the spatial proximity of spots
items.prompt: From spatial transcriptomics of 3 sections, we want a gene co-expression network in which each gene pair is weighted by how close in space the spots expressing them are.

items.core: communities that are spatially coherent across tissue regions
items.prompt: We have a TF-gene network built from spatial spots. Which method finds communities that are also spatially coherent, occupying contiguous regions of the tissue?

items.core: a network in which enhancers are the regulators of genes
items.prompt: We have H3K27ac and expression from 60 samples. We want a regulatory network in which enhancers, not TFs, are the regulators of each gene.

items.core: a network in which kinases regulate TF activity
items.prompt: We have phosphoproteomics and expression from 80 tumors. Is there a method that infers a network in which kinases regulate the activity of TFs through phosphorylation?

items.core: a federated learning setup across hospitals
items.prompt: We have expression, motifs and PPI from patients at three hospitals. We want a TF-gene network for each patient, and then a federated learning setup so the hospitals never share raw data.

items.core: automatic submission of the communities to a web database
items.prompt: Is there a method that finds the communities of our bipartite TF-gene network and then submits them automatically to a public web database?

items.core: learning the causal direction of each link
items.prompt: We have proteomics and metabolomics from 90 patients. We want a network of direct links between the two layers, and then the causal direction of each link.

items.core: TF protein quantification from mass spectra
items.prompt: With expression, motifs and PPI from 50 samples, we want each TF's activity per sample, and also each TF's protein amount quantified from our raw mass spectra.

items.core: a batch-corrected count matrix for later differential expression
items.prompt: We have expression from 140 samples run in four batches. We want the co-expression with batch effects removed, and also a batch-corrected count matrix for later differential expression.

items.core: per-patient networks with edges tested against the time point
items.prompt: We have expression, motifs and PPI from 90 patients, each sampled at one of three time points. We want a network for each patient and a test of which edges differ with the time point.

items.core: one network per developmental stage, compared between stages
items.prompt: We have expression from four developmental stages with motifs and PPI. Which method gives one regulatory network per stage so we can compare the stages?

items.core: a partition of a TF-gene network where each gene is in one community
items.prompt: We want to partition our bipartite TF-gene network so that every gene sits in exactly one community.

items.core: a network per biopsy compared across tumor regions
items.prompt: We took biopsies from four regions of each of 25 tumors, with motifs and PPI. We want a regulatory network for each biopsy so we can compare the regions.

items.core: direct links between methylation and expression at baseline
items.prompt: In 100 patients we measured methylation and expression at baseline. Is there a method that finds the direct links between the two layers?

items.core: per-sample TF activity related to treatment time points
items.prompt: We have 60 samples collected across five treatment time points, with motifs and PPI. We want each TF's activity in every sample to see which TFs change over the course of treatment.

items.core: co-expression differences between early and late stage, adjusted for sex
items.prompt: Which method shows how co-expression differs between early and late disease stage in our 130 samples, after adjusting for sex?

items.core: a co-expression network for each sample from several brain regions
items.prompt: We have expression from 6 brain regions of 15 donors. We want a separate co-expression network for each sample.

items.core: one TF and miRNA network at a single time point
items.prompt: At a single time point after infection we profiled mRNA and miRNA in 70 samples. We want one regulatory network with both TFs and miRNAs as regulators.

items.core: pathway-level mutation subtypes compared on five-year survival
items.prompt: We have somatic mutations for 320 patients with five years of follow-up. Is there a method that subtypes the patients from pathway-level mutation scores and compares survival between the subtypes?

items.core: a cohort TF-gene network for 30,000 genes within limited memory
items.prompt: We want one TF-gene network for 30,000 genes from 400 samples, but our machine has little memory. Which method fits?

items.core: how central each gene is inside its community
items.prompt: After finding communities in our TF-gene network, we want to know which genes are most central inside their own community.
